text:
Lukas Dostal has had a rough first month in Anaheim. He is 4-5-1 with an .858 save percentage, and he has allowed 4.6 more goals than his shots usually produce (goals saved above expected measures a goalie against the quality of shots he faces), in the 21st percentile among goalies. His last five appearances are worth -4.6, and two of them ended early: 20 minutes against Calgary and barely seven in St. Louis.

The trouble shows up at both ends of the danger range. He is stopping 93.0% of low-danger shots against a league 96.3%, and .648 on high-danger shots against a league .685. His medium-danger work has been better than average, which is something to build on.

How worried should Anaheim be? It depends on whose model you trust. Our numbers had him at -3.7 last season in 56 games, while Evolving-Hockey had him at +25.0, a gap that says a lot about how hard goalies are to measure. He played four games for Czechia at the Olympics in February. Twelve appearances is a small sample, and the next few starts will tell us whether this is a slump or a trend.
